## The 2014 transfer

The Social Science Data Archive transferred from UCLA's Social Sciences Division
to the UCLA Library via a Memorandum of Understanding, drafted and effective
November 1, 2014, and executed August 2015 (Virginia Steel, University Librarian,
2015-08-04; Alessandro Duranti, Dean of Social Sciences, 2015-08-10). The MOU
transferred:

- 2.0 FTE and approximately $245,000 in permanent funds
- Approximately $29,000 in permanent subscription funds (ICPSR, Roper, UC
  Berkeley/SDA, Colectica/Algenta)
- A "Data Archive Purchase Fund" foundation gift (~$10,477)
- Two staff with continuous service: Elizabeth "Libbie" Stephenson (Librarian)
  and Jina/Jamie Jamison (Programmer/Analyst), a director and a data archivist
  per the book chapter

The MOU also included a consultation clause: if the Library later made
"substantial changes to the operations of Social Sciences Data Archives," the
Library and the Social Sciences Division were to meet and ensure continuity of
faculty access to services.

By the 2010s, SSDA's narrow service profile (survey research data collection,
management, and preservation) no longer matched researchers' emerging needs
across formats (text, image, audio) and disciplines. The move to the Library was
framed as a way to modernize services rather than simply relocate an existing one.

Per Tim Dennis, Todd Grappone, then UCLA Library's AUL for Digital Initiatives
and Information Technology, shepherded SSDA's transfer into the Library. This
isn't yet documented in any source beyond Tim's own account as a direct
participant. Grappone later became University Librarian at UC Santa Barbara in
2025; see [People](people.qmd) for his fuller career record.

## The 2018 rebrand: Data Science Center

In Spring 2018, the unit was formally restructured and renamed the **Data Science
Center (DSC)**, with a new mission statement:

> The Data Science Center's mission is to foster a welcoming research community by
> developing data literacy and foundational coding skills through consulting and
> education. We support researchers throughout the full data life cycle of
> activities: planning research projects and data management plans; data
> acquisition, storage, cleaning and usage; analysis; publication; curation; and
> preservation.

The DSC retained SSDA's core services (data literacy, data management, data
discovery) while broadening scope to serve any discipline, not only the social
sciences. Per Tim, Todd Grappone also coined the "Data Science Center" name and
helped design and reorient the 2018 service model, alongside the 2018 book
chapter's co-authors.

## The Carpentries

The DSC joined **The Carpentries**, a volunteer-led data science teaching
organization, in 2017 (ahead of the formal 2018 rebrand) to scale instruction with
a limited staff. By the time of the book chapter's writing, Carpentries membership
at UCLA had grown to over ten instructors across six departments, including the
entire DSC team. Tim Dennis won The Carpentries' 2018 Community Service Award,
cited for teaching over 20 workshops and establishing Library Carpentry as a
Lesson Program within the organization.

## UCLA Dataverse

Before joining the Library, SSDA's collections lived on Harvard's hosted Dataverse
instance. In 2018, the DSC stood up a **local UCLA Dataverse** instance, extending
the same repository model (DDI metadata support, tiered curation, license
restriction) to the whole UCLA research community. Research groups can sponsor
their own branded sub-collections within it. Jina "Jamie" Jamison, whose UCLA
service traces back through the 2014 transfer, has led on UCLA Dataverse since:
she represented UCLA at the Dataverse Community Meeting 2021 and authored the
platform's preservation documentation.

## Staffing growth

The unit grew from two staff at the 2014 transfer to five full-time staff, adding
roles in GIS (Spatial Data Science Librarian), computational/data-science
facilitation, and machine learning. Most of that growth came from redesigning
existing library positions rather than net-new hiring, supplemented by a
Carpentries-trained instructor pool and a student program modeled on Carleton
College's DataSquad. Doug Daniels joined the DSC team in 2020 as Emerging
Technologies Librarian, folding the Lux Lab's 3D printing, scanning, and drone
mapping/imaging services into the center's portfolio; he won UCLA's 2026
Librarian of the Year Award for that work.

## A note on scope

This history stops at the DSC's structure as it stood before 2026. As of
publication, the unit's organizational status is under internal review. This
history does not attempt to characterize an unresolved process. It will be
revisited once that process concludes.
